task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi there! I'm having trouble with my mobile data — it either stops working completely or is just really slow. I'd really like to get it sorted out and get a nice fast connection on my phone. I don't have access to Wi-Fi right now, so mobile data is all I've got.

turns.thought: I can definitely help you get your mobile data working. First, I need to pull up your account — could you please confirm the phone number associated with your line, or your full name and date of birth?
turns.execution_output: User: Sure! My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002.

turns.thought:

- **Plan:** Premium Plan — 15 GB monthly data limit
- **Data used this cycle:** 15.1 GB of 15 GB (**limit exceeded**)

2. **Change to a plan with a higher data limit** — I can show you the available plans and their prices.

Which would you prefer?

Thanks for checking — I've verified on my end that the 2 GB refuel was successfully applied to line 555-123-2002 (your line now shows 15 GB plan + 2 GB refuel), the line status is **Active**, and **roaming is enabled**. There's also no overdue bill that would be blocking your service. So the remaining causes are on the device side.

Could you please try these steps on your phone and let me know what you see?

1. **Check the status bar** (top of screen) — look for an airplane icon ✈️ and signal bars.
   - If Airplane Mode is ON, turn it **OFF**.
2. **Confirm Mobile Data is turned ON** in Settings (Cellular / Mobile Network → Mobile Data).
3. **Check the network type** shown in the status bar — it should read 5G, LTE or 4G. If it shows 2G or 3G, let me know (older network modes can't carry data properly).
4. **Turn Data Saver OFF** if it's enabled, as it can throttle your speed.
5. **Reboot your phone**, then run the speed test again.

Please tell me what the status bar shows (airplane mode, signal strength, network type, data icon) and whether the speed test works after the reboot — and I'll take it from there. If we can't get it going with those steps, I'll escalate you to our technical support team so they can run deeper line/SIM diagnostics.

turns.thought:
Thanks — that's very helpful. Three things are likely holding you back: **mobile data is OFF**, the phone is locked to **2G** (which is far too slow for data, and can drop the connection entirely), and there's an **active VPN**. Please do these on your phone, in order:

1. **Turn Mobile Data ON** — Settings → Cellular / Mobile Network → Mobile Data (enable it).
2. **Change the network mode preference to 4G/5G preferred** — Settings → Cellular / Mobile Network → Network Mode (or Preferred Network Type), and select **4G/5G preferred**. Avoid 2G/3G-only options.
3. **Disconnect the VPN** — open your VPN app (or Settings → VPN) and disconnect it. VPNs can slow data significantly or block it outright.
4. **Reboot your phone**, then run the speed test again.

Also, your status bar shows **📶¹ Poor (1 bar)** signal. Even with everything set correctly, a single bar of signal in a weak-coverage spot can give you very slow or no data — if the speed test is still bad after the steps above, please try moving near a window or to a different location and re-test.

Let me know what the status bar shows after the reboot and what the speed test returns. If the network type is still stuck on 2G or you still have no connection, I'll escalate you to our technical support team to check the line and SIM further.
turns.execution_output: User: That's a lot of steps at once for me — I can only really do one thing at a time on my phone without getting mixed up. Could you walk me through them one at a time? Which one should I do first?

turns.thought:
Of course — one step at a time.

**Step 1: Turn Mobile Data ON**

1. Open your phone's **Settings** app.
2. Tap **Cellular** (it may be called **Mobile Network** or **Connections**, depending on your phone).
3. Tap **Mobile Data** and switch it **ON**.

You'll know it worked when the 📵 "Data Disabled" icon in your status bar is replaced by a 📱 "Data Enabled" icon (usually alongside the network type like 4G or 5G).

Go ahead and do that, then tell me what your status bar shows — no need to do anything else yet. Once data is enabled I'll walk you through the next step.

Mobile data is enabled now — that's step 1 done.

**Step 2: Switch the network mode to 4G/5G**

Your status bar still shows **2G**, and a 2G network is far too slow to carry mobile data — it's usually the reason the speed test fails outright.

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Cellular** (or **Mobile Network** / **Connections**).
3. Tap **Network Mode** — it may also be called **Preferred Network Type**.
4. Select **4G/5G preferred** (or "5G/LTE preferred"). Avoid any option that says 2G or 3G only.

Once selected, the network type in your status bar should change from **2G** to **4G**, **LTE** or **5G**.

Go ahead and make that change, then tell me what network type your status bar now shows. After that I'll take you through the next one — this time turning **Data Saver** off.

Excellent — that's a big improvement already: you're now on **5G with 4 bars of signal**, and data is enabled.

**Step 3: Turn Data Saver OFF**

Your status bar shows **🔽 Data Saver is on**. Data Saver restricts background data usage and can reduce your speed, so we should switch it off.

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Cellular** (or **Mobile Network** / **Connections**).
3. Tap **Data Saver** (it may be under **Data Usage**).
4. Switch it **OFF**.

You'll know it worked when the 🔽 Data Saver icon disappears from your status bar.

Do that, then tell me what your status bar shows. After this, the last item is the VPN — I'll walk you through that next.

Everything looks right now: **5G, 4 bars, data enabled, Data Saver off**. Let's see where that leaves us.

**Step 4: Run a speed test**

1. Open your browser or the speed test app on your phone.
2. Start a **speed test** and wait for it to finish.

Please tell me the result — specifically whether it now connects at all, and the speed it reports (e.g. very poor, poor, fair, good, or excellent).

- If it comes back **good or excellent**, we're done and your data is working.
- If it says **no connection** or comes back **slow**, we'll take one more look — the one remaining item is the **VPN** still showing as connected, which can throttle or block mobile data in some cases.

Go ahead and run the test, then let me know what it says.

That is frustrating — but you're right that everything on the status bar now looks correct. The one remaining item is the **VPN**, which is still showing as **Connected**. An active VPN routes all your traffic through a secure server, and if that server is slow or misconfigured it can block your data connection entirely — which would produce exactly the "no connection" result you're seeing, even with perfect 5G signal.

**Step 5: Disconnect the VPN**

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **VPN** (on some phones it's under **Network & Internet** or **Connections** → **VPN**).
3. You should see your VPN listed as connected — tap it and select **Disconnect**.
   - If you use a separate VPN app instead, open that app and tap **Disconnect** / **Turn Off** there.
4. Confirm the 🔒 VPN icon disappears from your status bar.

**Then run the speed test again** and tell me the result.

- If it comes back **good or excellent**, we're done.
- If it comes back **slow** or **still no connection**, let me know too — at that point I'd like you to **reboot your phone** (power it off and back on) and re-test, since a reboot refreshes all the network connections and often clears issues like this.

Go ahead and disconnect the VPN, then let me know what the speed test says.

I understand — you've been very patient working through all of these steps, and I'm sorry it's still not working. Let me double-check things on my end before asking you to do anything else, so we're not chasing the wrong thing.

I completely understand your frustration — you've done everything correctly and it still isn't connecting. I've just re-checked your line on my end and everything is in order: status **Active**, the **2 GB refuel** is applied, **roaming enabled**, and there's no past-due bill blocking service. So the issue isn't with your line or account.

Let's try the reboot, which is the last remaining step on the device side.

**Step 6: Reboot your phone**

1. Press and hold the **power button** (and volume button on some phones) until the power menu appears.
2. Tap **Restart** (or **Power off**, wait about 10 seconds, then hold the power button again to turn it back on).
3. Wait for the phone to fully start up and reconnect — give it about 30 seconds.
4. Check your status bar shows **📶 signal, 5G, and 📱 Data Enabled** again, then **run the speed test**.

A reboot refreshes all the phone's network connections and often clears issues that persist even when every setting looks correct.

Please try that and let me know the result. **If it still says "No Connection" after the reboot, stop there** — I'll escalate this to our technical support team, who can run deeper diagnostics on the line and SIM, since I've exhausted the steps available to me. I won't ask you to keep repeating anything.
